newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria seeks advisers for sale of state firms.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria seeks advisers for sale of state firms.

text.p: The Bulgarian government is seeking financial advisers for the planned sale of 22 state firms, including Balkan Airlines, the Neftochim refinery, shipyards and steelworks.
An announcement from the Privatisation Agency said bids for the enterprises would be invited from April 21, and banks and consultancies should apply by April 18.

Companies to be privatised include the Varna, Rousse and Bourgas shipyards, the Kremikovtsi and Stomana steelworks, fertiliser producer Neohim, motor vehicle producer Chavdar, and fuel distributor and retailer Petrol.

Many of the companies have been on the Privatisation Agency's list for some time. Russia's Rosneft has expressed an interest in buying a stake in Neftochim, but the Privatisation Agency suspended a previous attempt to privatise Balkan Airlines after it failed to find a buyer.
Privatisations are a key part of Bulgaria's commitments to the International Monetary Fund under a new standby agreement due to go before the IMF board in April for approval.

The privatisations will take place under the new government to be elected on April 19. The previous Socialist administration, ousted in February after a month of mass protests, was blamed for moving too slowly on privatisation.

On Wednesday, the Privatisation Agency supervisory board dismissed executive director Vesselin Blagoev, citing a lack of initiative and flexibility in the privatisation process and a lack of co-ordination between the agency's executive body and the supervisory board and government.
His successor is expected to be named this week.
